2607.06479.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Framework for Elastodynamic Wave Propagation in Bimaterial Systems
2607.06479.paper_summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) provide a promising framework for solving partial differential equations while embedding the underlying physical laws directly into the learning process. This study presents a PINN-based framework for modeling transient elastodynamic wave propagation in bimaterial systems governed by the axisymmetric equations of linear elasticity. A steel-aluminum specimen representative of a Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar configuration is considered, and the governing elastodynamic equations, together with the corresponding initial, boundary, and interface conditions, are incorporated directly into the network through a physics-informed loss function. High-fidelity finite-element simulations performed using ANSYS Workbench Explicit Dynamics are used for validation and as supplementary data constraints during training. The proposed framework accurately predicts wave transmission and reflection across the bimaterial interface and reproduces axial and radial displacement histories, face-averaged responses, and the dominant stress and strain evolution with close agreement to the finite-element solutions. The trained network further demonstrates the ability to predict wave responses at previously unseen time instants and for modified material properties without requiring additional finite-element simulations, providing a continuous surrogate model for elastodynamic analysis. Mesh-sensitivity studies confirm numerical robustness, while additional material combinations demonstrate the generality of the proposed methodology. The results show that integrating physics-informed neural networks with explicit finite-element analysis provides an accurate and computationally efficient framework for elastodynamic wave propagation in heterogeneous solids, offering an effective surrogate modeling approach for high-rate solid mechanics and impact engineering applications.
2607.06479.paper_summary_zh: 物理知識驅動的神經網絡（PINNs）提供了一個有前景的框架，用於解決偏微分方程，同時將基礎物理法則直接融入學習過程中。這項研究提出了一個基於PINN的框架，用於建模由線性彈性軸對稱方程所支配的雙材料系統中的瞬態彈動波傳播。考慮一個代表分裂霍普金森壓力杆配置的鋼-鋁樣本，並將支配的彈動方程及相應的初始、邊界和界面條件通過物理知識驅動的損失函數直接納入網絡中。使用ANSYS Workbench顯式動力學進行的高保真有限元素模擬用於驗證並作為訓練過程中的補充數據約束。所提出的框架準確預測了雙材料界面上的波傳遞和反射，並重現了軸向和徑向位移歷史、面平均響應以及主導應力和應變的演變，與有限元素解有著密切的一致性。訓練後的網絡進一步展示了在之前未見的時間瞬間和對修改材料性質的波響應進行預測的能力，而無需額外的有限元素模擬，提供了一個連續的彈動分析替代模型。網格敏感性研究確認了數值的穩健性，而其他材料組合則展示了所提出方法的普遍性。結果表明，將物理知識驅動的神經網絡與顯式有限元素分析相結合，為異質固體中的彈動波傳播提供了一個準確且計算效率高的框架，為高頻固體力學和衝擊工程應用提供了一種有效的替代建模方法。
